UPDATE 2026-07-29 (Docker, lyrical-theme-test): re-investigated with a correctly-identified live process (gdb-attached, PID/start-time verified via ps against a concurrently-running unrelated gz-sim-main from the same-day stability test). Over a ~34-minute window and two 20s-apart sample pairs of /world/oceans_waves/stats (the world's actual internal name, not the filename), iterations was continuously increasing -- this run never showed the zero-progress 4+ minute stall described above. Instead: sustained crawl at real_time_factor ~0.0008-0.0077 (mostly ~0.0018, lower than the 0.012-0.015 figure above), CPU ~31-32% (not the near-idle ~1% previously documented for Docker), and two gdb all-thread backtraces 30s apart showed the main thread's PC had moved (step-barrier wait -> inter-step nanosleep), independently confirming forward progress. Not a contradiction of the 2026-07-23 finding (that near-idle/zero-message observation was also real) so much as a second, different-looking failure mode on the same world -- may be RTF so low it's indistinguishable from a stall over a short sample. Async sonar compute thread read and ruled out as the blocker (does not gate PostUpdate); leading remaining suspect is the synchronous GPU ray-cast call (Render(), in upstream gz-rendering, likely slow under Docker's llvmpipe software rasterizer) -- not yet directly confirmed. See notes/results/dave_multibeam_sonar.log and README.md Progress Log 2026-07-23 and 2026-07-29. UPDATE 2026-07-31 (Mac, Metal, native): first same-world control measurement taken -- the identical world launched with no sonar sensor attached runs at RTF 0.9996 (544 samples, 60s), while with the sonar enabled at the default 10m range it runs at RTF 0.2223 (814 samples, 119.2s window, single confirmed instance, iterations 37,688 -> 64,188 monotonic). That is a ~4.5x slowdown against control -- neither the stall nor the ~80x crawl characterised on 2026-07-23, and 15-18x higher than that day's 0.012-0.015 Mac figure, which was not reproduced. Critical method caveat found the same day: the sonar sensor does not finish initialising until ~163s after launch on this machine (SONAR PLUGIN LOADED / '# of Beams = 513' / 'Persistent GPU buffers allocated for 513x301x399' appear only then); before that the world runs sonar-free at RTF ~1.0 while looking like a valid measurement. Six such readings were produced and discarded before the cause was identified. Docker has not been re-measured with this correction, so the 2026-07-29 figure (~0.0018) stands and is still ~123x worse than Mac -- consistent with the llvmpipe software-rasteriser suspicion but still unconfirmed. UPDATE 2026-08-03 (Mac, Metal, native): startup phase mapped continuously from t=0 to t=360s in back-to-back 25s windows (notes/results/multibeam_startup_2026-08-03/). This reproduces the 2026-07-23 stall symptom directly: for roughly 80 seconds (t~54-106s) /stats emits fewer than two messages per 25s window, versus 69-85 messages per window (~3.3 Hz) once healthy. One window at t=27s reads RTF 0.0014, the same order as the 0.012-0.015 figure, though that number rests on only two messages 0.711s apart and should be treated as indicative rather than a measured rate. From t=160s the sonar is live and RTF is flat across eight consecutive windows: mean 0.2060, min 0.1866, max 0.2219 -- matching the four 2026-07-31 repeats. Conclusion: the 2026-07-23 'livelock-like 4+ minute stall' on Mac is the world-load and sensor-init window, not a steady-state defect; that day's 25s and 90s settles both land inside it. Caveat: the startup curve is a single run, and it does not fully agree with 2026-07-31 -- there the pre-sonar window read RTF ~1.0 six times at 90-150s, whereas here t=133s already reads 0.1900. Sonar init time therefore varies by ~20-30s between runs, so 'pre-sonar means fast' is not reliable and only the post-init-confirmed measurement should be quoted. Docker still not re-measured; the ~0.0018 figure and the llvmpipe hypothesis are unchanged. UPDATE 2026-08-03 (Docker, lyrical-theme-test): the Docker figure is WITHDRAWN, not merely stale. Two findings. (1) The world no longer starts in Docker on either render engine: as shipped (<render_engine>ogre2 -- the ogre2->ogre patch this repo documents is NOT applied to the world files in that container) the sonar plugin loads (513 beams / 301 rays / 399) and then segfaults in Ogre2GpuRays::CreateSampleTexture() via CreateGpuRaysTextures/PreRender, null memcpy, exit 139, reproduced 2/2; patched to ogre it aborts earlier in RenderSystem_GL dllStartPlugin -> installPlugin -> __cxa_call_terminate, exit 134, never reaching the sensor. DISPLAY=:10 against the container's xrdp X socket did not change it (XAUTHORITY untested, so weak evidence). This is distinct from the 'Failed to load plugin [ogre2]' failure recorded elsewhere -- here ogre2 loads and reaches PreRender. (2) The 2026-07-29 measurement sampled /world/oceans_waves/stats and asserted that was this world's internal name. It is not: dave_multibeam_sonar.world declares <world name="default">, verified in both the Mac workspace and the container. oceans_waves is the internal name of dave_ocean_waves.world AND dave_ocean_waves_sonar.world, and the 2026-07-29 entry itself records a concurrent 4h dave_ocean_waves stability run in the same container. The wrong-PID issue was corrected that day, the topic name was not -- so the ~0.0018 RTF and the 'Docker ~123x worse than Mac' comparison are withdrawn. The gdb program-counter evidence from that day concerns the correct process and stands; the RTF numbers do not. There is currently NO valid Docker RTF measurement for this world and none can be taken until the crash is resolved. Write-up: notes/results/docker_multibeam_crash_2026-08-03/. Scripts: notes/experiments/ (go.sh 6). UPDATE 2026-08-03 (Mac, range sweep): sonar <range><max> varied 10/3/1 m, all else identical, sonar confirmed live each run. RTF 0.2186 / 0.2507 / 0.1933 -- not monotonic (1 m is the slowest, not the fastest) and the 1.30x spread barely exceeds the 1.19x fixed-setting noise floor. Range has no measurable effect. Together with the integrated-world measurement the same day, no axis varied on Mac moves this number: scene content, world and range all give 0.19-0.25, while sonar present vs absent gives 0.9996 -> ~0.22. The ~4.5x cost looks fixed per frame. Caveats: n=1 per range; only <max> was changed, not <maxDistance> (also 10) or <raySkips>, so if the work loop keys off maxDistance this test is blind -- unchecked in source. Next axis: ray/point count (exp1b). Data: notes/results/range_sweep_2026-08-03/. UPDATE 2026-08-05 (Mac): the ~4.5x sonar cost is ~90% proportional to ray count. Sweep: 153600 rays -> RTF 0.2180, 30720 -> 0.5017, 7680 -> 0.6632, 960 -> 0.6835 (no-sonar control 0.9996). In cost terms (1/RTF minus control) a line fitted through only the two largest points, overhead = 0.345 + 2.111e-5 x N, predicts the 7680 point to within 0.2%. At the default configuration that is 10% fixed / 90% ray-proportional. Not settled: extrapolating to zero rays still leaves an RTF ceiling of 0.744, so ~a quarter of the slowdown is fixed and unexplained; and linear-in-N does not distinguish the Render() ray-cast from FillPointCloudMsg -- raySkips separates compute rays from emitted points and is the untested discriminator. n=1 per condition. METHOD CHANGE: log lines are no longer used as the settle signal. Direct sampling showed the simulator does essentially nothing for the first ~60-75s (iterations 8 -> 11 between t=30s and t=60s) then steps at ~9000 per 30s, and no log line marks that transition; over 2026-08-03 the sonar log timings drifted 163s -> 20s while the frozen phase stayed the same. common.sh now waits on iterations growth. Consequence: the 2026-08-03 exp1 (range) and exp4 (integrated) figures were taken under the old criterion and should be re-run. Data: notes/results/raycount_2026-08-05/. UPDATE 2026-08-05 (Mac, re-measured under the stepping criterion): the 2026-08-03 range result is CORRECTED. New sweep 10 m 0.2100 / 3 m 0.2156 / 1 m 0.2344 is monotonic in the expected direction, where the earlier run was non-monotonic and was recorded as 'no measurable effect'. In overhead terms a 10x range reduction removes 13%, against 72% for a 5x ray reduction. Range therefore has a small real effect roughly an order of magnitude weaker than ray count; 'irrelevant' is withdrawn, but it remains not the explanation for the ~4.5x cost. Only <max> was varied, not <maxDistance> or <raySkips>. Data: notes/results/remeasure_2026-08-05/. UPDATE 2026-08-05 (Mac, raySkips): the sonar compute stage is NOT the bottleneck. raySkips subsamples rays at the compute stage only, leaving the 513x301 raycast intact; effective ray counts confirmed from the plugin log (301/31/11/4/2). Increasing compute ~10x raises overhead 3.785 -> 6.559 (+73%, positive control passes), but reducing it 15.5x changes nothing (3.635-4.649, a 1.28x spread against a 1.19x noise floor, no trend). Linear fit through the endpoints: overhead = 3.466 + 0.01028 x compute_rays, so compute contributes only 8% at the default setting. Combined with exp1b (beams/rays 5x cut gave -72%), the gain there came from the GPU raycast and/or the PointCloud2 fill, not the backscatter/matmul/FFT path. Raycast and point count are coupled by beams/rays in the SDF, so no further configuration sweep can separate them -- next step is profiling or reading MultibeamSonarSensor.cc. Unexplained: the 4- and 2-ray points sit ~1.1 above the fit. n=1 per condition. Data: notes/results/rayskips_2026-08-05/. UPDATE 2026-08-05 (Mac, Release rebuild): roughly two thirds of the sonar cost was build configuration. All 14 DAVE packages have CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE and CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS empty in CMakeCache.txt and no package CMakeLists sets them, so nothing is compiled with -O. Rebuilding multibeam_sonar and multibeam_sonar_system with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (verified -O3 in compile_commands.json) takes the default 153600-ray configuration from RTF 0.2180 to 0.4380, a 2.01x speed-up removing 64% of the overhead. gz-rendering was not rebuilt, so the gain is plugin-side by construction and the per-ray marginal cost fell 6.1x -- the ray-proportional cost is in plugin code, consistent with FillPointCloudMsg. The relation also went from linear (as shipped) to sub-linear (-O3). CONSEQUENCE: the 0.19-0.22 figures from 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-05 describe the unoptimised build and are superseded for Release builds; the README reproduction section produces an unoptimised build and should be fixed. A real cost remains: 0.438 vs the 0.9996 control is still ~2.3x. Caveat: the as-shipped build was never directly confirmed -O0, only inferred from the empty cache entries. Data: notes/results/release_rebuild_2026-08-05/.
